rows.speaker: عنبسة
rows.claim: ʿAnbasa reports that Ibn Shibrima challenged Dhu al-Rumma’s line as saying love had departed, and the poet changed لم يكد to لم أجد.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عنبسة أنه قال : قدم ذو الرمة الكوفة ، فوقف ينشد الناس الكناسة

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: The narrator’s father says Ibn Shibrima was wrong to object and Dhu al-Rumma wrong to revise: لم يكد does not assert that love had departed.
rows.anchor: حدثت أبي قال : أخطأ ابن شبرمة حين أنكر على ذي الرمة ، وأخطأ ذو ذو الرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Common usage applies ما كاد or لم يكد to an act eventually done only with difficulty, or one whose occurrence seemed unlikely; that usage prompts the mistaken reading.
rows.anchor: قد جرى في العرف أن يقال : ما كاد يفعل ، ولم يكد يفعل : في فعل قد فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjani argues that literally لم يكد means the act did not occur or even approach occurrence: since كاد marks near occurrence, negating it cannot affirm completion.
rows.anchor: فإن الذي يقتضيه اللفظ إذا قيل : لم يكد يفعل ، وما كاد يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After denying that the Prophet can make hardened unbelievers hear, the exception إن أنت إلا نذير addresses them as if they doubt that he can do more than warn.
rows.anchor: ما أنت بمسمع من في القبور إن أنت إلا نذير

words: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement إن أنا إلا نذير وبشير similarly follows a denial of powers, so the preceding discourse makes the exception-form apt rather than a bare positive assertion.
rows.anchor: قل لا أملك لنفسي نفعا ولا ضرا إلا ما شاء الله ولو كنت أعلم الغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنما affirms an action for one person and denies that same action of another at once; جاءني زيد لا عمرو presents the two ideas in sequence.
rows.anchor: اعلم أنها تفيد في الكلام بعدها إيجاب الفعل لشيء ، ونفيه عن غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second advantage of إنما is that it makes the named person’s responsibility for the action more explicit than simple coordination with لا.
rows.anchor: وهي أنها تجعل الأمر ظاهرا في أن الجائي زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In جاءني زيد لا عمرو, لا removes the particular arrival in question from Amr and assigns it to Zayd; it does not deny that Amr ever came too.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى أن ليس المعنى في قولك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The correction assumes the listener knows that someone came but mistakenly attributes that arrival to Amr; the speaker identifies Zayd as the one who came.
rows.anchor: ونكتة أخرى وهي أنك لا تقول : جاءني زيد لا عمر و ، حتى يكون قد بلغ المخاطب أنه كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjani extends this analysis to إنما: it corrects who performed the mentioned action without implying that no one accompanied Zayd.
rows.anchor: وإذ قد عرفت هذه المعاني في الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reading إنما as explicitly saying Zayd alone came from the whole group is possible only with added wording like وحده; that restriction is contrived in ordinary usage.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك شيء كالتكلف ، والكلام هو الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurjani attributes the flaws in lines criticized for bad composition, including examples attributed to al-Mutanabbi and Abu Tammam, to violating the rules governing order, omission, and related choices.
rows.anchor: وفي نظائر ذلك مما وصفوه بفساد النظم ، وعابوه من جهة سوء التأليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correctness and excellence in composition likewise come from following those rules; نظم consists in observing the relations and meanings that govern words together.
rows.anchor: ثبت أن ليس هو شيئا غير توخي معاني هذا العلم وأحكامه فيما بين الكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ellipsis can be more eloquent than explicit mention: silence may convey more, making speech most expressive precisely when something is left unsaid.
rows.anchor: فإنك ترى به ترك الذكر ، أفصح من الذكر ، والصمت عن الإفادة ، أزيد للإفادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited line ربع قواء أذاع المعصرات به, an omitted demonstrative or predicate is understood: ذاك ربع قواء or هو ربع.
rows.anchor: ربع قواء أذاع المعصرات به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line about Marwa’s house omits an opening demonstrative, understood as تلك دار.
rows.anchor: دار لمروة إذ أهلي وأهلهم بالكانسية نرعى اللهو والغزلا

rows.speaker: شيخنا
rows.claim: His teacher rejects parsing الربع as a substitute for الطلل: a substitute must equal or exceed its antecedent, whereas a quarter is larger than a ruin trace.
rows.anchor: قال شيخنا رحمه الله : ولم يحمل البيت الأول على أن الربع بدل من الطلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poets also omit verbs: the accusative ديار in the cited line is understood as governed by an omitted verb, أذكر ديار مية.
rows.anchor: أنشده بنصب ' ديار ' على إضمار فعل ؛ كأنه قال : أذكر ديار مية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A common ellipsis occurs at a cut or fresh start: after introducing a person and some details, poets begin a new sentence with its predicate but omit its subject.
rows.anchor: ومن المواضع التي يطرد فيها حذف المبتدأ القطع والاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Word order should not be divided into cases where it carries meaning and cases where it is mere poetic license; a placement that adds a benefit does so consistently.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن من الخطأ أن يقسم الأمر في تقديم الشيء وتأخيره قسمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With hamza questions, verb-first أفعلت asks whether the act occurred, while noun-first أأنت فعلت asks who performed it.
rows.anchor: إذا قلت : أفعلت ؟ فبدأت بالفعل كان الشك في الفعل نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Prophet a shining lamp is metaphorical for being illuminating; the sensory lamp image makes the expression more vivid.
rows.anchor: السراج ها هنا مستعار وحقيقته مبينا , والاستعارة أبلغ للإحالة على ما يظهر بالحاسة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling death a resting place metaphorically likens resurrection to waking; repeated human experience of sleep and waking makes this image more vivid than death and life.
rows.anchor: أصل الرقاد النوم وحقيقته من مهلكنا , والاستعارة أبلغ لأن النوم أظهر من الموت ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image of people surging like water means their mingling, and is stronger because water exemplifies powerful mixing.
rows.anchor: أصل الموج للماء وحقيقته تخليط بعضهم ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the wind barren means it brings no rain cloud; the metaphor is stronger because failure from an opposing condition is especially clear.
rows.anchor: العقيم مستعار للريح , وحقيقته ريح لا يأتي بها سحاب غيث ,

words: ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hand tied to the neck metaphorically means withholding generosity; the physical image makes the disliked restraint more vivid.
rows.anchor: حقيقته لا تمنع نائلك كل المنع والاستعارة أبلغ لأنه جعل منع النائل بمنزلة غل اليد إلى العنق

words: من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To taste punishment means to be punished; the metaphor is stronger because tasting is active sensory seeking, and pain is cast as a taste normally associated with pleasure.
rows.anchor: حقيقته لنعذبنهم , والاستعارة أبلغ , لأن إحساس الذائق أقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that God prevented their ears from sensation without making them deaf.
rows.anchor: حقيقته منعناهم الإحساس بآذانهم من غير صمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphor compares silencing the ears to striking a book shut; ears are named rather than eyes because closed eyes can still reopen, whereas blocked hearing prevents awakening.
rows.anchor: وإنما دل على عدم الإحساس بالضرب على الآذان دون الضرب على الأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نكسوا على رؤوسهم metaphorically describes lowering their heads in humiliation when the proof bound them, intensifying the image as a fall from bewilderment.
rows.anchor: هذا استعارة , حقيقته أطرقوا للمذلة عند لزوم الحجة ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سقط في أيديهم means they regretted seeing the grounds for regret; its sensory image exposes the bad choice and its consequences.
rows.anchor: هذا مستعار وحقيقته: ندموا لما رأوا من أسباب الندم ,

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rummani defines harmony as balanced arrangement of letters and distinguishes dissonant composition, middle harmony, and the highest harmony.
rows.anchor: التلاؤم نقيض التنافر , والتلاؤم تعديل الحروف في التأليف , والتأليف على ثلاثة أوجه:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an as a whole occupies the highest tier of harmonious composition, distinguishable on close consideration from all other speech.
rows.anchor: والمتلائم في الطبقة العليا القرآن كله , وذلك بين لمن تأمله.

rows.speaker: ذكروا
rows.claim: Some attribute the قبر حرب line to jinn: its consonant discord makes it difficult to recite three times without stumbling.
rows.anchor: وذكروا أن هذا من أشعار الجن لأنه لا يتهيأ لأحد أن ينشده ثلاث مرات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s verse about being struck by love illustrates the middle, still pleasing level of harmonious composition.
rows.anchor: وأما التأليف المتلائم في الطبقة الوسطى - وهو من أحسنها - فكقول الشاعر:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People differ in their sensitivity to harmony and dissonance by natural temperament, like their differing ability to hear sound meter or distinguish forms and characters.
rows.anchor: وبعض الناس أشد إحساسا بذلك وفطنة من بعض

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil explains dissonance as either excessive distance or excessive closeness between letters; both impede the tongue, while moderation makes speech easy.
rows.anchor: ما ذكره الخليل من البعد الشديد أو القرب الشديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harmony pleases the ear, eases pronunciation, and helps the mind accept meaning through attractive form and indication.
rows.anchor: والفائدة في التلاؤم حسن الكلام في السمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same meaning resembles a book read in beautiful or ugly handwriting: its image varies, and that variation affects reception.
rows.anchor: ومثل ذلك مثل قراءة الكتاب في أحسن ما يكون من الخط والحروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction: Jabir heard only the later revelation episode, not its beginning, so he supposed al-Muddaththir was first; it was first after Iqra.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن جابرا سمع من النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - هذه القصة الأخيرة ولم يسمع أولها فتوهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Jabir transmits the Prophet’s account after the hiatus: he heard a heavenly voice, saw the Hira angel between heaven and earth, was terrified and covered, then received al-Muddaththir; al-Bukhari and Muslim narrate it.
rows.anchor: عن جابر قال: سمعت النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report shows that revelation paused after Iqra and then resumed with يا أيها المدثر; the Hira angel episode therefore occurred after Iqra.
rows.anchor: وبان بهذا الحديث أن الوحي كان قد فتر بعد نزول

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn reports Iqra as the first Meccan revelation; he gives al-Mu’minun or al-Ankabut as the last Meccan surah, al-Mutaffifin first in Medina, Bara’a last there, and al-Najm as the first surah taught in Mecca.
rows.anchor: علي بن الحسين يقول: أول سورة نزلت

words: إن الله لا يغفر أن يشرك به ويغفر ما دون ذلك
rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn calls 78:30 the harshest verse for Hell’s inhabitants and 4:48 the most hopeful verse for people affirming God’s unity.
rows.anchor: سمعت علي بن الحسين يقول

words: واتقوا يوما ترجعون فيه إلى الله
rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn identifies 2:281 as the last verse revealed and says the Prophet lived nine nights afterward.
rows.anchor: سمعت علي بن الحسين يقول
